title: Zip the Little Snail
targetPhonics: CVC short i and short u, consonant blends
skill: CVC words with short i (Zip, big, hid, did) and short u (mud, run, fun, sun)
skill_description: Practice reading CVC words with short i and short u sounds while enjoying a story about friendship
author: FunBookies

story_bible.premise: Zip is a little purple snail who wishes he could move fast like his best friend Hop the frog. When a big storm rolls in and everyone rushes to find shelter, Zip worries he'll be left behind. But his slow, careful path leads him to discover the perfect cozy hiding spot—and when Hop gets stuck in the mud, Zip's patient, steady help is exactly what saves the day.
themes: everyone moves at their own pace

character_arcs.Zip: Wishes he was fast → Worries during the storm → Finds perfect hiding spot → Saves his friend → Realizes slow is just right
character_arcs.Hop: Fast and carefree → Rushes in the storm → Gets stuck in mud → Grateful for Zip's help → Appreciates Zip's pace

story_bible.setting: A sunny meadow with a pond, tall grass, wildflowers, and a cozy forest edge. The story moves from bright sunshine to dramatic storm clouds to peaceful aftermath. Colors are warm greens, sunny yellows, stormy grays, and warm sunset oranges at the end.
story_bible.plot_summary:
Zip the snail and Hop the frog are best friends, but Zip always feels slow compared to Hop who can jump and leap so fast. One sunny day, dark clouds roll in and a big storm is coming! All the animals rush to find shelter.

Hop zooms off toward the forest, but Zip can only inch along slowly. "I am too slow!" Zip thinks sadly. But as he moves carefully through the grass, Zip spots something the rushing animals missed—a perfect cozy log, dry and safe!

Zip slides inside just as the rain begins. But then he hears a cry: "Help! I am stuck!" It's Hop! In his rush, Hop jumped right into thick mud and can't get out.

Zip inches back out into the rain. Slowly, patiently, he reaches Hop. "Grab my shell," Zip says. Bit by bit, pull by pull, Zip helps Hop out of the mud. Together they slide into the cozy log.

"You saved me!" Hop says. "Your slow way was just right." Zip smiles. Maybe being slow isn't so bad after all. When the sun comes out, the two friends sit together, happy. Zip doesn't wish to be fast anymore. He's just right the way he is.

emotional_beats.beat: Joy - Zip and Hop playing in the sunny meadow
Longing - Zip watching Hop jump fast, wishing he could too
Worry - Storm clouds rolling in, animals rushing
Sadness - Zip left behind as others rush away
Discovery - Zip finds the perfect cozy log
Alarm - Hearing Hop cry for help
Determination - Zip going back out into the rain
Effort - Slowly, patiently pulling Hop from mud
Relief - Both safe in the cozy log
Contentment - Friends together in the sunshine

story_bible.level_adaptation: Simplified to CVC words (Zip, hop, run, mud, hid, big, got, fun, sun) and short sentences. Key phonics: short i (Zip, big, hid, did, bit), short u (mud, run, fun, sun, stuck). Emotional complexity preserved through expressive illustrations.

parent_tips.before_reading: Look at the cover. Ask: What animals do you see? How do you think snails move? Have you ever felt like you couldn't keep up with others? This book practices short i and short u words.
parent_tips.during_reading: Help your child sound out CVC words: Zip, hop, run, mud, big, hid, got, sun. Notice the difference between 'fast' and 'slow'. Use different voices for Zip and Hop!
parent_tips.after_reading: Discuss: Why was Zip sad at first? How did being slow help Zip? What did Hop learn about his friend? What makes YOU special, even if it's different from others?

reference_prompt:
9-PANEL STYLE REFERENCE SHEET for children's picture book "Zip the Little Snail"

Row 1 - MAIN CHARACTERS:
[1] ZIP THE SNAIL: Small purple snail with bright orange swirly shell, big soulful dark eyes, gentle smile, tiny antenna with dots at tips. Soft, friendly design. Cream background.
[2] ZIP EXPRESSIONS: Same purple snail showing three emotions - sad/wistful (looking up longingly), determined/brave (moving forward), happy/proud (big smile, content)
[3] HOP THE FROG: Bright green frog with darker green spots, big cheerful yellow eyes, wide friendly smile, long jumping legs. Energetic pose mid-hop.

Row 2 - CHARACTER INTERACTIONS AND KEY OBJECT:
[4] HOP EXPRESSIONS: Same green frog showing - jumping joyfully, panicked/stuck (wide scared eyes, reaching out), grateful/happy (looking at friend warmly)
[5] **CENTER HERO SHOT**: Zip the purple snail and Hop the green frog TOGETHER side by side - clear size contrast, both smiling, friendship moment. THE KEY IMAGE.
[6] THE COZY LOG: Hollow log with rounded entrance, dry cozy inside with soft moss, surrounded by ferns and grass. Warm, safe feeling.

Row 3 - SETTINGS:
[7] SUNNY MEADOW: Bright cheerful meadow with tall green grass, yellow and white wildflowers, warm sunshine, blue sky with fluffy clouds. Happy, peaceful.
[8] STORMY WEATHER: Same meadow but with dark gray storm clouds, rain falling, wind blowing grass, dramatic but not scary. Puddles and mud visible.
[9] AFTER THE STORM: Golden sunset light over fresh meadow, rainbow in distance, everything glistening, peaceful warm mood. Hope and happiness.

STYLE: Cheerful watercolor illustration style. Soft edges, friendly rounded character shapes. Bright greens and yellows for happy scenes, dramatic grays for storm, warm golden tones for resolution. Child-friendly, gentle, expressive.

LAYOUT: 3x3 grid, thin white borders between panels.

CRITICAL: NO TEXT, NO WORDS, NO LETTERS anywhere in the image. Pure illustration only.
